summary: Phase 149O.20J.4 -- Class-B Full Ancestor-Chain Verification Repair Independent Verification: independently verified 149O.20J.3's repair of B-149O.20J.2-1 from primary contracts and fixed Git source, not from 149O.20J.3's report or test suite. Reconstructed the exact pre-repair _ancestor_chain_safe from git show 72eaa241^:src/pcae/core/hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py (verbatim extraction) and executed it against a real fixture (grandparent agent-writable, parent mode 0o555 proven-safe, subject mode 0o555): result True, stops at the parent boundary, grandparent never inspected -- historical defect independently reproduced. The same fixture against current production source returns False, correctly detecting the writable grandparent. Independently re-derived HBDC-REQ-017/020's ancestor trust boundary before reading 149O.20J.3's own claim in detail: HBDC-REQ-020's directory-entry-replacement threat composes recursively at every ancestor depth (a writable ancestor at any level can replace the entry naming everything beneath it, regardless of how many proven-safe ancestors sit between it and Protected Root); no document in this repository names an intermediate architecture-defined trust anchor between Protected Root and the filesystem root; CBD-3/CBD-7 require the ACL/parent-path channel fully closed and fail-closed on indeterminate evidence. Concluded the filesystem root is the only contract-supportable boundary, independently converging with 149O.20J.3's own conclusion. Adjudicated that 149O.20H section 11's original terminating-walk design ('does not need to prove every ancestor up to /') was a genuine design error refuted by its own directory-entry-replacement mechanics, root-causing B-149O.20J.2-1 -- not a legitimate alternative contract reading. Inspected the current repaired _ancestor_chain_safe structurally and by control flow: no early return on a locally-safe result, unsafe ancestors reject immediately, indeterminate ancestors never resolve to True, loop-guard exhaustion fails closed, diagnostics record every traversed ancestor, and no caller can inject a weaker boundary. Wrote a fresh 25-test independent module (tests/test_phase_149o_20j_4_class_b_full_ancestor_chain_verification_repair_independent_verification.py), not copied or renamed from the J.3 suite, executed against real chmod/ACL/symlink filesystem state with all stubbing (for this dev host's own agent-writable ancestry above any tmp_path fixture) explicitly documented in-line. Attacks covered and PASSING: immediate-parent-writable, safe-parent-plus-writable-grandparent (the decisive B-149O.20J.2-1 case), 4 independently-exercised higher levels, fully-safe-chain positive case (stable across repeated runs), effective-GID-only higher-ancestor write (composed end-to-end with J-2's real _current_agent_identity via a monkeypatched os.getgroups() that explicitly excludes the real gid), symlinked higher ancestor (constructed real-symlink chain), inspection-error and indeterminate-ACL injection above a safe ancestor (both force overall None, never True), Trusted-Git and Protected-Root complete-walk semantics (both independently attacked with a writable-grandparent fixture and confirmed to pass the target path into the shared primitive unmodified, via inspect.getsource -- not assumed from symbol identity), and the real host's continued non-COMPLIANT result. ONE ATTACK CLASS DOES NOT PASS, and is NOT the B-149O.20J.2-1 early-stop defect: ACL-only higher-ancestor write on macOS. Ground truth (verified by directly creating/deleting a probe file through the ACL grant alone): chmod +a 'user allow add_file,delete_child' on a directory with mode 0o555 (no POSIX write bit anywhere) grants real, exploitable directory-entry-replacement authority. _acl_grants_agent_write_macos (unchanged by 149O.20J.3, pre-existing) detects an ACL grant only via the literal substring 'write' in `ls -lde` output; macOS canonicalizes directory ACL rights to add_file/add_subdirectory/delete_child (independently confirmed: even `chmod +a '... allow write'` on a directory is silently rewritten by the OS to add_file in the stored/displayed ACL) -- none of which contain 'write' -- so a real ACL-only directory-entry-replacement grant on any ancestor is never detected, tracked as new finding B-149O.20J.4-1. Verified two ways (direct primitive call and full ancestor-walk with everything else in the chain proven/stubbed safe): both currently marked xfail(strict=True) in the new module so the suite stays green while the finding remains loudly disclosed rather than silently skipped. File-level ACL evaluation (Trusted Git's own executable check) is unaffected -- a file's write right displays literally as 'write'; only directory ACL rights are canonicalized away from that substring. Root-caused why this escaped every prior phase: every existing ACL-only-higher-ancestor test in this repository (149O.20J.3's own test_live_acl_only_higher_ancestor_write_rejected, 149O.20J.2's test_git_deep_ancestor_acl_only_grant_bounded_by_first_safe_boundary, and the 149O.20I-era tests) monkeypatches _acl_grants_agent_write directly to a fake function rather than exercising the real ls -lde-parsing implementation against a genuine OS-level ACL grant -- confirmed via git grep that this phase's own test file is the only one in the repository that ever calls a real chmod +a. An honest test-design gap, not deliberate concealment, but the reason a real bypass persisted through J-3's prior closure determination. Re-verified J-1 (hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py confirmed byte-unchanged via git diff --stat since before 149O.20J.3, not report assertion) and J-2 (_current_agent_identity still independently folds os.getegid(), re-confirmed end-to-end); J-3's file-level ACL awareness remains closed, its ancestor-level ACL awareness is now known-incomplete per B-149O.20J.4-1 (not a regression -- the primitive predates 149O.20J.3 and was never actually exercised against real ACL state before this phase). Independently reconstructed the exact J.3 production diff via git diff --name-only 72eaa241^ 72eaa241 -- src/: exactly hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py; hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py and hatp_class_b_conformance.py confirmed byte-unchanged across the full four-commit J.3 range; of the four J.3 commits only 72eaa241 touches src/, c029a5f1 touches only the test file, the remaining two are report/lifecycle-metadata-only. Confirmed HMIC frozen scope unchanged: _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES still exactly 25 entries (none of the three Class-B verifier modules present), _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES still exactly 5 members. Zero production consumers reconfirmed via git grep. Read-only/no-mutation wall reconfirmed via source inspection (no chmod/chown/mkdir/makedirs/rmtree/remove/unlink/file-write call in either module). Real-host result unchanged: verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() returns non-COMPLIANT; git status byte-identical before/after this phase's test execution. Fast Green clean-deselected citation: 0 failed, 6771 passed, 5 skipped, 1 pre-existing unrelated collection error (fido2 missing); raw run 71 failed (none in the new J.4 test file) -- deselected via an argv-list subprocess call, not shell interpolation. Narrow broad sweep (class_b or hbdc or 149o_20j): 11 pre-existing fixed-commit self-checks or intentionally-superseded historical assertions, zero delta attributable to this phase. No production source file changed by this phase -- git status confirms only the new test module prior to report/metadata/status-doc updates. ADJUDICATIONS: B-149O.20J.2-1 (the early-stop bypass specifically): INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT NON-AUTHORITATIVE VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY -- does not imply HMIC binding, deployment, readiness, or operational closure. B-149O.20J.4-1 (new): OPEN -- BLOCKING for any claim that HBDC-REQ-016/017/020's ACL channel is closed on macOS. J-1/J-2 REMAIN INDEPENDENTLY CLOSED. J-3 file-level closed; ancestor-level ACL awareness known-incomplete, not reopened as a regression. CBV-S1: OPEN -- HMIC SOURCE-SCOPE BINDING STILL PENDING; this phase does not HMIC-bind anything. CBV-S10: OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT/INTEGRATION GAP, unchanged. Class-B: CONTRACT VERIFIED -- VERIFIER IMPLEMENTATION INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED FOR THE EARLY-STOP DEFECT -- ONE KNOWN OPEN ACL-DETECTION GAP (B-149O.20J.4-1) -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize real provisioning, certification, activation, HMIC scope evolution, or readiness integration, and does not perform the B-149O.20J.4-1 repair itself (no governed verification-phase rule was located authorizing an in-phase bounded repair of a defect outside B-149O.20J.2-1's own named scope). Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_4_CLASS_B_FULL_ANCESTOR_CHAIN_VERIFICATION_REPAIR_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md documenting methodology, historical reproduction, boundary derivation, attack-matrix results, the B-149O.20J.4-1 finding and its root-cause analysis, regression results, governance close checks, and all adjudications. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20J.3 to a new stacked Previous Phase entry) and CHANGELOG.md. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20J.5 -- Class-B ACL-Only Higher-Ancestor Detection Repair (macOS) -- repair _acl_grants_agent_write_macos's right-name matching, re-verify against real chmod +a grants, add a permanent real-ACL regression test. Not authorized by this phase. 149O.20K should only be reconsidered once 149O.20J.5 is independently verified, and must still perform its own fresh HMIC-REQ-052 transitive authority-dependency closure analysis.
